title: How a page edit is supposed to go
body:
A page edit is one pass through the same four calls, in order. The agent decides the content; the tools decide whether the write is allowed and record it.

1. query {"slug": "<slug>"} - read the page and note its revision.
2. validate {"instance": {title, slug, body}} - check the draft without storing it. Fix anything in errors[] before going on.
3. mutate with the default dry run: {"action": "update", "slug": "<slug>", "page": {...}, "expectedRevision": "<revision from step 1>"}. Nothing is written; the result shows the page and proposed revision.
4. mutate again with "dryRun": false and an "idempotencyKey", then query to confirm.

Creating a page skips the expectedRevision. Update and delete require it. If the result is a conflict, someone else changed the page: re-read with query, re-apply the edit on the current page, and try again. Never retry a conflict with a stale revision.

Every real mutate lands in the journal (strumentario journal, or the strumentario://journal resource) with the agent id, the revisions before and after, and a hash of what was submitted. Pages hold the content; the journal holds the act.

Do not edit the JSON files in the data directory by hand: that bypasses validation, revision checks and the journal.
